- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior peak.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–10 days; apply downward correction of 3–8% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment turns positive after a downtrend (e.g., +0.3+), model frequently underestimates upside; increase forecast by 1–4% to capture momentum.
- Model consistently underestimates true outcomes when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.0–0.3) — adjust upward by 1–3% for such periods.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 5 days show mean reversion (price oscillating within ±2% of 14-day moving avg), model tends to overpredict; cap forecast at 1.5–2% above recent range.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating +/–0.3), model often fails to capture short-term reversals — use 3-day rolling average to smooth and anchor forecast.
